chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
He was asked about a man who gives an advance payment (salam) for sheep, specifically two-year-olds and one-year-olds, and other than that, up to a specified term.

He said: There is no problem if the one upon whom is the sheep is not able to provide all of what is upon him, that the owner of the sheep takes half of it, or a third of it, or two-thirds of it, and they take the capital value of what remains from the sheep in dirhams, and they take below their stipulation, and they do not take above their stipulation.
And garments are also like wheat, and barley, and saffron, and sheep.
ai.seo_question: What are the rules for partial delivery in a salam contract if the seller cannot provide the full quantity?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the flexibility of the 'salam' contract in Shia jurisprudence, permitting partial delivery of livestock or agricultural goods when the seller is unable to fulfill the entire obligation. It establishes that the buyer may accept a proportional share of the actual goods and receive the monetary value of the remainder, provided the total compensation does not exceed the agreed-upon terms. This ruling underscores the practical application of fairness in trade, ensuring that neither party is unduly burdened by partial performance.
